pointers.sentence: `BaseModelAdmin.get_fieldsets` returns the option `fieldsets` if it is set, else one unnamed fieldset of `BaseModelAdmin.get_fields` (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:BaseModelAdmin.get_fieldsets`).

`get_fields` returns `fields` if set; else it builds a form, `get_form` with no fields, and returns the names of its `BaseForm.base_fields` and then the read-only names (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:BaseModelAdmin.get_fields`).

The auth application's `UserAdmin` overrides `get_fieldsets` and `get_form` so that its add page has `UserAdmin.add_fieldsets` and `UserAdmin.add_form` (`django/contrib/auth/admin.py:UserAdmin.get_fieldsets`, `django/contrib/auth/admin.py:UserAdmin.get_form`).

The form is subclassed with `type` under its own name, each read-only name it declares as a field set to `None`, which `DeclarativeFieldsMetaclass` takes to drop the field (`django/forms/forms.py:DeclarativeFieldsMetaclass.__new__`).
Fields still `None`, with a form whose Meta names neither fields nor exclusions, become `ALL_FIELDS` (`django/forms/models.py:modelform_defines_fields`).

`BaseModelAdmin.__init__` makes the entries, merging each of the class's `formfield_overrides` into a copy of `FORMFIELD_FOR_DBFIELD_DEFAULTS`, the admin's widgets by model field class, "rather than simply overwriting" (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:BaseModelAdmin.__init__`).

`formfield_for_foreignkey` and `formfield_for_manytomany` choose a widget only when none was passed: by `get_autocomplete_fields`, then `raw_id_fields`, then `radio_fields` for a foreign key, or `filter_vertical` and `filter_horizontal` for a many-to-many (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:BaseModelAdmin.formfield_for_foreignkey`, `django/contrib/admin/options.py:BaseModelAdmin.formfield_for_manytomany`).

`formfield_for_foreignkey` and `formfield_for_manytomany` choose a widget only when none was passed: by `get_autocomplete_fields`, then `raw_id_fields`, then `radio_fields` for a foreign key, or `filter_vertical` and `filter_horizontal` for a many-to-many (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:BaseModelAdmin.formfield_for_foreignkey`, `django/contrib/admin/options.py:BaseModelAdmin.formfield_for_manytomany`).

The queryset, unless passed, is `BaseModelAdmin.get_field_queryset`'s: the related model's default manager, ordered by the related model admin's `BaseModelAdmin.get_ordering` and not filtered by its `BaseModelAdmin.get_queryset`; with no model admin or no ordering, `None`, and the model field makes its own (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:BaseModelAdmin.get_field_queryset`).

The change form wraps the form in an `AdminForm`, with the fieldsets, the prepopulated fields and the read-only names, which on a view-only form are every name of the fieldsets (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin._changeform_view`, `django/contrib/admin/helpers.py:AdminForm`).

`AdminErrorList` puts the errors of a bound form and of its inline formsets in one list, whose length chooses "error" or "errors" in the note above the fieldsets (`django/contrib/admin/helpers.py:AdminErrorList`).
`AdminReadonlyField` finds a read-only field's label and value itself (`django/contrib/admin/helpers.py:AdminReadonlyField`).

The value is `lookup_field`'s: a model field's value, or what a callable, a method of the model admin, or an attribute or method of the model gives for the object (`django/contrib/admin/utils.py:lookup_field`).

`Fieldset.is_collapsible` is true when `"collapse"` occurs in the string of its classes and no name of the fieldset's `"fields"` has an error, so a group that holds an error opens (`django/contrib/admin/helpers.py:Fieldset.is_collapsible`).
